what_its_for: This kit is used by your healthcare team to safely collect and store the blood from your baby's umbilical cord right after birth. Cord blood is rich in special stem cells that can be used to treat certain blood diseases, immune system disorders, and some types of cancer — either for your child or a matching family member in the future. It can be stored in a cord blood bank for possible use later.
how_to_take: You do not use this kit yourself. Only trained doctors, nurses, or midwives will handle the collection. Right after your baby is born and the umbilical cord is cut, your healthcare provider will use this sterile kit to draw blood from the cord into the collection bag. The process takes only about 5 to 10 minutes and is completely painless for you and your baby. The collected blood is then sealed, labeled, and sent to a cord blood bank for processing and storage.
dosing: There is no 'dosing' for this product. The amount of cord blood collected is determined naturally — usually between 40 and 150 milliliters (about 3 to 10 tablespoons). Your healthcare provider will collect as much cord blood as is safely available. The volume collected will be recorded on your kit label.
missed_dose: Because cord blood can only be collected immediately after birth, there is no opportunity to reschedule or repeat the collection. If for any reason the collection could not be completed at the time of delivery — for example, due to a medical emergency — it cannot be done at a later time. Talk to your doctor before your due date to make sure the team is prepared to collect cord blood at delivery.
storage: Once the cord blood is collected, it must be kept at room temperature (between 59°F and 86°F / 15°C to 30°C) and sent to the cord blood bank within 48 hours of collection. Do not freeze the collection bag before it reaches the bank. Keep the sealed kit away from direct sunlight and extreme heat or cold. Before the birth, store the unused collection kit at room temperature, away from moisture and out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Do not open or touch the sterile collection bag or tubing — this must remain sterile until your healthcare provider uses it. Do not attempt to collect cord blood yourself at home. Avoid storing the unused kit in very hot or cold places (like a car trunk or freezer). Do not delay sending the collected cord blood to the bank — time is critical for keeping the stem cells healthy.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or midwife right away if: the collection kit bag or packaging appears damaged, torn, or opened before use; the collection bag leaks or is damaged after collection; you are unsure how to get the collected sample to the bank on time; you have questions about whether cord blood banking is right for your family; or if your delivery plans change and you need to update your birth team about the cord blood collection.
when_it_works: The cord blood is processed at the bank within a few days of collection. Successful storage means the stem cells are safely frozen and preserved — sometimes for 20 years or more. If the stored cord blood ever needs to be used for treatment, the bank will thaw and prepare it at that time. Your family will receive a report confirming successful storage, usually within a few weeks after delivery.
special_populations: Cord blood collection is safe for all full-term and most preterm pregnancies, but the amount collected may be smaller with premature births. If you have a high-risk pregnancy, multiple births (twins, triplets), or certain infections like HIV or hepatitis, talk to your doctor about whether cord blood banking is appropriate for you. Some conditions in the mother or baby may affect the quality or usability of the collected cord blood. Always inform your healthcare team of any medical conditions before your due date.
